drafted_from: tool:run-better-auth-sign-in's row and tools/better-auth (README, settings.json, src/main.rs); the answers below were observed by building it (cargo build --release) and running it on this checkout's code with port 38791 and a synthetic account
start_here: Say to your AI: "Start my Better Auth sign-in server on port 8791 with tools/better-auth/settings.json and check it answers at http://localhost:8791/api/auth/ok."
no_lists_because: It names no list of yours: it keeps its users, sessions, passkeys and signing keys in its own SQLite file (settings.json database_path), not in Trillion rows.
instructions: 1. The AI reads the row with run_resource_operation at @workshop-tools, tools:list { tool: "tool:run-better-auth-sign-in" } and clones https://github.com/Trillion-X/trillion-workshop.git on your computer.

2. Edit trillion-workshop/tools/better-auth/settings.json for your port, base_url, issuer, audience, passkey origin and database file; set BETTER_AUTH_SECRET from your vault by name (32+ random characters, never printed) and RUST_ICU_MAJOR_VERSION_NUMBER=78 with RUST_ICU_LINK_SEARCH_DIR at ICU 78's lib folder (brew install icu4c@78).

3. Run cargo run --release --quiet --manifest-path trillion-workshop/tools/better-auth/Cargo.toml --target-dir /tmp/better-auth-build -- trillion-workshop/tools/better-auth/settings.json; the first build takes a few minutes.

4. Check GET {base_url}/api/auth/ok answers {"ok":true}; sign up with POST /api/auth/sign-up/email, get a JWT with GET /api/auth/token (cookie or Authorization: Bearer) and give verifiers {base_url}/api/auth/jwks.

worked_examples.title: Start it, sign up one person and read their token
worked_examples.ask: Start my sign-in server and make a test account for Sam.
worked_examples.given: Observed on this computer: settings.json with port 38791 and base_url http://localhost:38791, run as the row's command; then curl POST http://localhost:38791/api/auth/sign-up/email {"email":"sam@example.com","password":"correct-horse-battery-9","name":"Sam"} and GET /api/auth/token with Authorization: Bearer <the session token>.
worked_examples.hands_back: GET /api/auth/ok answered {"ok":true}. Sign-up answered {"token":"<a 32-character session token>","user":{"name":"Sam","email":"sam@example.com","emailVerified":false,"image":null,"id":"<32 characters>"}}. GET /api/auth/token answered {"token":"eyJhbGciOiJFZERTQSIsImtpZCI6..."}, an EdDSA JWT whose kid matches GET /api/auth/jwks {"keys":[{"alg":"EdDSA","crv":"Ed25519","kty":"OKP","x":"...","kid":"..."}]}.
